answers.note: I'd like to explore this a bit more, I like both options 2 and 3. Let's preserve those and continue finding more disposable camera designs that can define Partyreel. Really marketable feature, needs to be cool.

However, it'd be ideal if this was a reversible filter so the original media is preserved, but we're not creating two storage copies of every image with a separate stylized version. If we can simply apply filters to the original unmodified media, that'd be the ideal solution so it can be swapped/turned off anytime.

This should be a host config so they can either choose immediate uploads/visibility or set a 'develop' time guests can see to get them excited and in the loop. It creates that 'return' payoff moment where everyone sees the final album. If this isn't an upcoming question for me, I'd like to ask you: how do disposables best work with the live reel, or reels/clips in general? Seems like if implemented wrong, disposables kills the 'reel' side of Partyreel, which is very bad. Would reels be limited to the 'develop' moment, when the 'reel' itself develops? Maybe host has slideshow access either way to play live at event to encourage usage, but guests just don't have reel or gallery until they 'develop' and can then watch/clip/etc? Sorry, bit of a ramble here.

This is not a direct selection, more what I think leads to the coolest idea. The darkroom effect of this option inspired an idea to effectively make this an atmospheric 'waiting room', where there's a live count (reasonable server usage) as new media is added. There could be an intriguing mystery stack of media in the center, make the 'waiting room' a fullscreen experience. A guest should also have access to their uploads from this screen, maybe even their uploaded media becomes the media stack in the waiting room with a way to manage (like delete an upload). Really excited to see your creative ideas here too, don't get locked to mine.

This is likely one of the biggest choices to make for an event, so it deserves its own focused step for hosts to make that decision with plenty of context for each experience-type provided. Question: would these two types be easily interchangeable later on an event, or should the selection in the create step be a one-way door into that mode per event? Ideally, it's very streamlined for hosts to switch between if they'd like, so if a host changes their mind last minute despite having everything set up ("i've already printed QRs and texted links, but i wish i chose uploads instead of disposables" - easy swap), we don't tell them 'sorry, have to make a new event from scratch'.

Let me know if you disagree, but I think beyond the obvious choice of 'storage decides' to maintain our current pricing, we should go 'at full size'. If i'm a host, I'd rather have the original resolution images from my event and pay a little extra for more storage if needed, rather than intentionally receive reduced quality media. If not already handled somewhere, videos should also work in pro disposable events.

I'd like to carry over the album's own camera and the camera that shoots on a reel (options 1 and 3). Let's also branch 2 new design ideas from each. I love the more minimalist camera design of the first, where everything is immediately understandable, UI is amazingly clear, and subtle design touches like the tick count around the shot button are a nice touch. However, the reel idea really ties into the product as well, and makes it a little more fun/novel as you take pictures. My main pushback on this one may be the reel having a more vintage feel within our far more modern app design, which is only getting sleeker as we iterate.

These are so much cooler than the current host dashboard, standard event pages for both host and guest, and other areas of our app. Really creates a bespoke, experiential feeling. Going off my previous notes about wanting to redesign most of our app and especially breaking away from the shadcn generic AI build feel, this is the kind of creativity I like to see. I'd like to see another round of these to get the best option - by one note is that for grids, I'd prefer not to get messy and begin tilting anything, the slight rotation may make us feel too playful for more sophisticated events.
This makes it way more fun so everyone can see what's happening as the event goes on. Builds the excitement publicly for when the album develops later for everyone to access.
I love keeping the host within the 'develop' experience initially, but also offering them an easy skip to check the album out. Could probably polish this design more.

The pictures help immediately visualize the distinct experiences, with light copy to clearly define. Should also have an option to compare more deeply somehow. However, the entire create wizard, including this screen, needs to be redesigned and polished. Lots going on. Many parts could be reshaped into more minimal yet high-info-conveyance UI, very text heavy right now.

Can we revisit the roll looks/styles idea, whether with a live preview in Chrome through Orchestrator or with some examples of how it's being used in the lab or something? I'm not sure I want to include - feels like filters are going to make the majority of guest photos worse that don't match the palette well.
